scope: Independent visual review of the 20 expanded neutral staff-diagnostic rows only, across 11 source pages and 4 PDFs. All 40 before/after strips and 11 original context images were viewed. No production edits, new native worker, musical instrument-assignment certification or whole-score recall claim.

summary.verdict: Preservation holds for the changed edges; substantial additional neighboring notation in 18 rows is an explicit cleanliness cost. These are not 18 proven target-note recoveries and the diagnostic strips are not publication-ready isolated parts.

limitations: The original target/instrument assignments are not resolved by these neutral profiles; no claim is made that one detected staff equals a complete instrumental part.
No full-part output pagination or page-turn review is included. Taller contaminated rows can consume more output space.
Existing clipped neighboring glyphs, shared directions outside these local crops, faint scan ink and source-relative recall outside the changed edges remain unresolved.

Six diagnostic PNG overlaps are pixel-exact; fourteen differ after mapping their pixel origins. Independent clipped rasterization is the likely cause, but not separately isolated here. Pixelwise PNG equality is not used as the preservation oracle; the bound unchanged source and exact strict-superset PDF rectangles supply that evidence.
